The company

Same system

One model. The laptop and the phone.

Imagine OS is the same session on both screens. The illustrated layout below is the product direction. The live model is the demonstration further down. Release 0.0.1 runs that model locally.

Proof

Run a model in this browser.

Press the button and a small open model loads into WebAssembly on this device. Nothing is typed in for you, and the tokens are the model’s. This is SmolLM2 135M Instruct at Q4_K_M, not the 20-billion-parameter target. The first run downloads the weights from Hugging Face. Generation is capped at 64 tokens, and after the weights are in memory it does not call a server.

A Hugging Face example is coming soon.

Energy and performance

        
The model spends the machine’s own power.

        

          Boole keeps inference on the device so the work does not travel to a
          cluster. What follows is what release 0.0.1 actually does. Anything
          else is a design goal. The only measured speed we have is from the
          browser demo: 12.3 tok/s for SmolLM2-135M Instruct Q4_K_M, 64 tokens,
          on a 4-core Xeon CPU in WebAssembly, one thread, no GPU layers.
        

        

          

            Quantization
            
Smaller weights, same file format.

            

              Aliases resolve to GGUF quants from Q2_K through Q8_0. Bits per
              weight are estimated in the hardware package, from 3.35 for Q2_K
              to 8.50 for Q8_0.
            

          

          

            Memory
            
Pick the quant that fits.

            

              boole run reads free RAM, reserves a 2 GB headroom,
              and chooses the highest-quality quant that still fits. If none
              fits, it stops and says so. doctor prints the same verdict.
            

          

          

            CPU and GPU
            
Offload when the build can.

            

              The CLI calls getLlama({ gpu: 'auto' }). That runtime
              uses Metal, CUDA, or Vulkan when the prebuilt binary matches the
              machine, and the CPU when it does not. --gpu-layers
              sets a layer count. Omit it and the runtime decides.
            

          

          

            Threads
            
Not exposed in 0.0.1.

            

              The command line does not set a thread count. The browser demo
              does: one WebAssembly thread and zero GPU layers. Choosing threads
              for a resident runtime is a design goal.
            

          

          

            Idle
            
The process exits, and the model goes with it.

            

              There is no long-running server. serve is reserved
              and not implemented. A resident runtime that unloads the model
              when it is idle is a design goal, not a behavior of this release.
            

          

          

            Network
            
Generation reads the local file.

            

              Token sampling uses the GGUF on disk. The prompt is not uploaded.
              Release 0.0.1 still asks Hugging Face for the file name before it
              opens the cache, so a cached boole run is not fully
              offline yet. Weights download only when they are missing.

Architecture

        
How a local run works.

        

          

            boole run takes an alias, such as llama3, or a
            repository and quantization. The alias resolves to a GGUF file that
            fits the memory this machine reports. If that file is not in the
            cache, pull downloads it from Hugging Face and resumes
            if the transfer stops. node-llama-cpp then loads the file, opens a
            context, and samples tokens in-process. Standard output is the
            model text. Diagnostics stay on standard error.

Privacy and security

        
What stays here, and what does not.

        

          

            
The command line

            

              The published source has no analytics call. Network code
              resolves and, when needed, downloads a model file from
              Hugging Face. That lookup runs before the cache check, including
              on boole run. A prompt is passed to the local session.
              The CLI does not sign or attest the weights. You are trusting
              the repository the alias, or you, selected.
            

          

          

            
This page

            

              The runtime and the page are static. The model file is fetched
              only after you press the button, from one public Hugging Face
              URL. During generation the page counts new network requests and
              reports that count. There is no account and no telemetry pixel.
              This is not a security certification.

Questions

        
Answered up front.

        

          

            What is Imagine OS?
            
Imagine OS is the product Boole AI, Inc. is building: software shaped around the person using it, with the model running on the device. Release 0.0.1 is the local command-line runtime. The shell that keeps adapting is the direction of the company.

          



            What runs today, and what is still a roadmap?
            
Today you can run a local GGUF model with boole run, pull, doctor, and models. The browser demo runs SmolLM2 135M in WebAssembly. Ternary weights, a 20B model at 200 tok/s, phones, NPUs, and an adapting shell are goals. They are not measured results and not commitments.

          



            Which devices does it support?
            
The command-line runtime follows node-llama-cpp 3.22.2 prebuilt binaries: macOS Apple Silicon with Metal, macOS Intel on CPU, Windows and Linux x64 with CUDA, Vulkan, or CPU, Linux arm64 and Windows arm64 on CPU, plus Linux armv7l and riscv64 CPU prebuilts. The demo runs in a modern browser with WebAssembly. iOS, Android, NPUs, and other edge devices are a 24-month roadmap, not support today.

          



            Where does my data go?
            
A prompt is passed to the local session. The CLI has no analytics call. It does contact Hugging Face to resolve a model file name before it opens the cache, and it downloads weights when they are not cached. Token generation reads the local GGUF. The page demo fetches weights only after you press the button, then counts network requests during generation.

          



            What do managed and white-glove include?
            
Pay to start is Imagine OS as a managed product. Boole AI stands it up, deploys it, and keeps it running with continuous uptime. White-glove means that setup and service are done by Boole AI. The scope of that service is agreed when you start. There is no published uptime percentage.

          



            How does acquiring the codebase work?
            
It is a full inquiry, not an instant checkout. Write to hello@booleinference.com with the subject “Boole: Codebase acquisition”. Full ownership of the code and the technology is settled in a written agreement. It is a deliberate process.

          



            What license is the software under?
            
The software is proprietary to Boole AI, Inc. All rights reserved. Use, copying, modification, and distribution require a written license or agreement. Earlier public releases were published under the MIT License.

          



            How do I contact Boole AI?
            
Email hello@booleinference.com. Pay to start uses the subject “Boole: Buy now”. A codebase inquiry uses “Boole: Codebase acquisition”. A general call uses “Boole: Book a call”.
